key_insight: World Tracing bridges the gap between pixel-faithful depth estimation and complete 3D generation by predicting geometry that stays aligned with the input image while extending beyond what is directly visible.
problem_solved: Existing image-to-3D methods face a trade-off: depth methods are accurate to visible pixels but incomplete, while generative 3D methods produce full shapes that can drift away from the image. This paper tackles the challenge of generating complete 3D geometry without losing pixel alignment.
method: Introduces a generative pixel-aligned geometry representation called World Tracing.
For each input pixel, predicts an ordered stack of camera-space 3D points rather than only a single depth value.
Uses the stacked geometry to model both visible surfaces and occluded/completed structure beyond the visible region.
impact: This approach can improve 3D reconstruction from single images by making outputs both faithful to the input and more complete. It is especially useful for practitioners building view synthesis, scene understanding, robotics, and image-to-3D systems that need reliable geometry.

paper_title: World Tracing: Generative Pixel-Aligned Geometry Beyond the Visible
paper_authors: Hao Zhang, Mohamed El Banani, Jen-Hao Cheng, Paul Zhang, Yi Hua
